findings_qualitative.value: Clear detection of blueshifted and redshifted 12CO (J = 3-2) emission associated with MMS-1

evidence.quote: We have clearly detected the blueshifted and redshifted emission of the ^{12}CO (J = 3–2) at MMS-1 (Figure 1 (a,b)) for the first time at the present high-angular resolution.

findings_qualitative.value: Non-detection of dense gas tracers H13CO+ and C17O toward MMS-1, indicating absence of connecting high-density envelope

evidence.quote: It is to be noted that we cannot detect high-density tracers, H^{13}CO^{+} (J = 3–2) and C^{17}O (J = 3–2), toward MMS-1 even with the higher angular resolution compared with Paper II.

findings_qualitative.value: The compact and detached disk suggests mass accretion onto the protostar/disk may have halted recently

evidence.loc: A detached disk at the center of an isolated protostellar core
evidence.quote: The observed disk in MMS-1 is very small, indicating that further significant mass accretion through the disk does not occur anymore. Thus, we may be witnessing a stage close to the moment when the accretion activity has been halting.

claims.hypothesis: Does the very low-luminosity protostar in MC27/L1521F have a rotating circumstellar disk and what is the mass of the central object?
claims.experiment: High-angular resolution (~0.18" x 0.10") ALMA Band 7 continuum and 12CO (J = 3-2) observations of MMS-1 in MC27/L1521F compared with synthetic Keplerian disk models
claims.result: Detected compact 12CO velocity gradient with highest velocity ~7 km/s at ~2 au, fitted by Keplerian disk model with M_* = 0.18 +/- 0.05 M_sun, R_disk = 9 au, and M_disk = 8 x 10^-5 M_sun
claims.finding: The VeLLO MMS-1 hosts a compact rotating Keplerian disk with a central protostellar mass of ~0.2 M_sun and disk mass of ~10^-4 M_sun

evidence.quote: The spatial/velocity distributions of the gas show there is a rotating disk with a size scale of ~10 AU, a disk mass of ~10^{-4} M_{\odot} and a central stellar mass of ~0.2 M_{\odot}.

claims.hypothesis: Is the protostellar disk actively fed by an extended connecting dense envelope?
claims.experiment: High-resolution imaging of high-density molecular tracers H13CO+ (J=4-3) and C17O (J=3-2) and dust continuum around MMS-1
claims.result: No high-density line emission detected toward MMS-1, and no extended high-density envelope connecting to the disk in 0.87 mm continuum
claims.finding: The disk appears detached from the surrounding envelope, potentially truncated by turbulent dynamical interactions in the core

evidence.quote: It is to be noted that we cannot detect high-density tracers, H^{13}CO^{+} (J = 3–2) and C^{17}O (J = 3–2), toward MMS-1 even with the higher angular resolution compared with Paper II. These results indicate that the disk may be detached from the surrounding environment although it is located at the center of the dense core whose density is ~10^6 cm^{-3}.

claims.hypothesis: Can the extremely low luminosity (<0.1 L_sun) of a ~0.2 M_sun protostar be reconciled with stellar evolution models?
claims.experiment: Pre-main-sequence evolutionary calculation with cold accretion starting from a 0.01 M_sun core
claims.result: Standard pre-main-sequence tracks require >1 Myr to reach <0.1 L_sun, whereas cold accretion models reproduce ~0.07 L_sun within <10^5 yr with R_init ~ 0.65 R_sun
claims.finding: The low luminosity of ~0.07 L_sun for a ~0.2 M_sun protostar can be matched within <10^5 yr if accretion occurred via cold accretion with an unusually small initial stellar radius (~0.65 R_sun)

evidence.quote: However, we cannot explain the observed low luminosity with the standard pre-main-sequence evolutionary track unless we assume cold accretion with an extremely small initial radius of the protostar (~0.65 R_\odot).

why_this_method.value: Synthetic ALMA observations of Keplerian disk models with CASA simobserve and simanalyze were needed to deconvolve beam dilution effects on unresolved/marginally resolved disk kinematics

evidence.loc: Physical quantities of disk of MMS-1
evidence.quote: since the present ALMA observations do not have a sufficient resolution to spatially resolve the disk structure, the comparisons with the simulation of rotating disks are needed to remove the effect of the beam dilution.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Standard pre-main-sequence evolutionary tracks cannot explain the observed low luminosity (<0.1 L_sun) for a ~0.2 M_sun protostar within dense core timescales

evidence.loc: A very low-luminosity object as a candidate evolved by cold accretion
evidence.quote: According to the classical evolutionary tracks of pre-main-sequence stars (cite: Baraffe98), it takes >1 Myr for a ~0.2 M_{\odot} protostar to reach a luminosity of <0.1 L_{\odot}.

limitations_admitted.value: Disk structure is not fully spatially resolved at ~20 au resolution, requiring simulation comparisons to correct for beam dilution

evidence.loc: Physical quantities of disk of MMS-1

limitations_admitted.value: Models include only the disk and not the surrounding dense core envelope or absorption

evidence.loc: Physical quantities of disk of MMS-1
evidence.quote: We note that we simulated only the disk component, although the source is heavily embedded in a dense core. This difference is seen in the spectrum mainly around the systemic velocity (4.45–9.55 km s^{-1}); the dense core is observed in this velocity range.

referee_caveats_inferred: The disk is only marginally resolved, so derived stellar mass and radius depend heavily on the adopted Keplerian thin disk geometry and fixed inclination.
Forefront core absorption obscures the line profile near systemic velocity, limiting constraints to the high-velocity wings.
